news.title: England-Republic of Ireland U15 World Cup game ends over alleged racism
news.lede: England players gathered at the side of the pitch after the alleged incident. England walked off the pitch during a match at the Under-15 World Cup after an allegation of racism by a Republic of Ireland player, which resulted in the game being abandoned. Following an altercation between players from both sides, shortly before the end of the match in Azerbaijan on Monday, an England player approached his bench and made a complaint to coaching staff. Match footage then showed England staff members relaying the complaint to the referee, alleging a racist slur had been said, and calling their players off.

news.title: Northern Ireland women’s football squad welcomed to Galgorm Resort ahead of Portugal World Cup play-off
news.lede: Galgorm Collection welcomed Northern Ireland’s senior women’s football team to Galgorm Resort recently as the squad prepared for its FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 European qualifying play-off against Portugal. Northern Ireland’s senior women’s football team enjoyed a stay at Galgorm Resort near Ballymena as they prepared for their FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 qualifying play-off against Portugal earlier this month. The national squad and coaching staff were welcomed to the Co Antrim resort ahead of the first-leg encounter at Inver Park in Larne on Friday 9 October, with the visit highlighting the ongoing relationship between Galgorm Collection and the Irish Football Association (Irish FA). The resort provided accommodation and facilities for the players and coaching team as they focused on preparations for the international fixture.

news.title: England U15s stars storm off pitch after alleged racist incident in World Cup clash vs Ireland
news.lede: ENGLAND’S UNDER-15s walked off the pitch during their World Cup match against Ireland due to an alleged incident of racism. Young Lions boss Matt Thorpe withdrew his players in the 40th minute of Monday afternoon’s match. The Daily Mail reports that an England player claimed an opponent had allegedly made a racist comment towards him. A member of the Irish backroom staff reportedly shouted, ‘No, he didn’t,’ while the English player protested back.

news.title: From 12,000 players assessed to 14 selected for Azerbaijan, how India are building a scouting network to
news.lede: India's search for the next generation of football talent has taken a step forward, with the country's U-15 team continuing its winning run at the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival Azerbaijan 2026. The Blue Colts beat Cameroon 2-1 in their second Group K match in Baku on Sunday, but the result is also part of a much bigger effort to identify and develop young footballers across the country.Over the past two years, the All India Football Federation (AIFF) has assessed more than 12,000 players from across India as it looks to identify promising talent and prepare them for the future. The initiative was originally designed to find players born in 2011 and 2012 and develop them through AIFF-FIFA talent academies.
